content:
maria: Hey team — saw a weird latency pattern on canary this morning. 95th jumped ~40% between 03:10–03:20 UTC.
aj: perf-bot alerted too. Any chance it's probe/autotune churn?
perf-bot: alert: route=lm-infer-canary model=gpt-small region=us-west-2 metric=latency_95 delta=+42% threshold=20%
devon: I pulled a sample. Sequence length skewed — a sudden tail of seq=512 requests. Our kernel-decider picked large-batch Triton path then failed over to CUTLASS; fallback added ~30ms.
maria: snippet from logs:
```
[kernel-decider] seq=512 chosen=triton_large fail=true reason=kernel_timeout runtime=812ms fallback=cutlass_fast runtime_after_fallback=850ms
```
oliver: hmm fallback runtime is slower than triton timeout — indicates probe timing mismatch. Are we still using the 10-sample probe window for seqlen buckets?
devon: yes, probe window=10, sample-rate=0.5. If heavy tail arrives, early probes bias toward the tail and flip the arbiter.
aj: I think the autotune hysteresis isn't strong enough. We flip on 3/10 votes. Suggest 5/10 + 30s cooldown.
maria: also KV cache impact — those seq=512s were mostly cold-cache (new user sessions). Cold KV means triton large batch misses more often.
oliver: concrete action: (1) increase probe threshold to 5/10 (2) add cooldown 30s (3) log histogram of seq by cache-hit for 1 hour. I'll open a PR.
devon: PR #4287 opened: https://redwood/repo/pulls/4287 — contains heuristics change + a debug toggle to force probe sampling.
sre-bot: note: scheduling canary rollback window remains 1h. Recommend extending to 2h until we validate churn reduction.
maria: can we also tweak the fallback path latency cap? If fallback > +15% then don't switch for at least 60s.
aj: agreed. I'll prototype cap in the decision function and run local perf harness.
oliver: i'll schedule a quick blast test at 09:00 PT and collect traces. tagging @perf to prioritize.
perf-bot: perfjob queued: job=kernel-blast-1939876543 status=queued
maria: thanks. keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the change. Will post post-mortem if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
